entities.summary: Hillah, also spelled Hilla, is a city in central Iraq. On the Hilla branch of the Euphrates River, it is 100 km (62 mi) south of Baghdad. The population was estimated to be about 455,700 in 2018. It is the capital of Babylon Province and is situated in a predominantly agricultural region which is extensively irrigated with water provided by the Hilla canal, producing a wide range of crops, fruit and textiles. Its name may be derived from the word "beauty" in Arabic. The river runs in the middle of the town, and it is surrounded by date palm trees and other forms of arid vegetation, reducing the harmful effects of dust and desert wind.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a major agricultural center in medieval West Asia, Hillah played a crucial role in supporting the population of Baghdad and surrounding regions through its extensive irrigation system. The city's strategic location along the Euphrates River made it an important hub for trade and commerce.
